These charts are drafts for the slide deck. Each slide section shows the chart and the
numbers worth quoting. The same chart is saved as a PNG in
`analysis/marshall_requests/png/`.

## Data files

**From the data library** (`Public_Data_Library`):

- **Crime (slides 3 and 16):**
  `analysis/fbi/srs/fbi_srs_estimated_crimes_state.rds`
- **Population (slides 5, 8, 10 and 16):**
  `analysis/census/pep/census_pep_state.rds`
- **Prison admissions and population (slides 6, 8, 13, 14 and 22):**
  BJS National Prisoner Statistics, 1978–2022 (ICPSR 38871), in `raw/bjs/nps/`,
  and `analysis/bjs/prisoners_series/prisoners_by_jurisdiction.csv` for 2023
- **Probation (slide 10):**
  `analysis/bjs/ppus/adults_on_probation_by_jurisdiction.csv`
- **Correctional officers (slide 13):**
  `analysis/bls/oews/bls_oews_state.rds`
- **Corrections spending (slide 14):**
  `raw/nasbo/se/1991-2022 State Expenditure Report Data.xlsm`

**From elsewhere:**

- **Arrests (slides 4, 5 and 7):**
  the FBI Crime Data Explorer API, saved in `data/cde-arrests-national.csv`.
  Renders read that file. Delete it to pull again, which needs `DATA_GOV_API_KEY`.
- **Recidivism (slides 9 and 16):**
  CSG's 50 States, 1 Goal file, `2026_50_state_1_goal_long_update.csv`, in SharePoint under
  `z_ARCHIVE/50 State Revocations Project/State Recidivism Compendium/data for analysis/`
- **National recidivism studies (slide 9 alternatives):**
  `data/recidivism-national-studies.csv`, typed in from the published BJS and Pew reports.
  It has one row per study, with the report name and a link.
- **Missouri (slide 22):**
  `data/missouri-jr.csv`, typed in from the Missouri Department of Corrections'
  *Profile of the Institutional and Supervised Offender Population, FY2025*
  (tables 1.4 and 4.2), fiscal 2016–2025. Without this file the slide falls back to BJS counts.
- **Prison health care (slide 13d):**
  `data/health-care-costs.csv`, typed in from Pew and Vera's *Prison Health Care: Costs and
  Quality* (2017), appendix C tables C.1 and C.3, fiscal 2010–2015. The report PDF is saved in
  the project's `data/` folder.
- **Inflation (slides 13 and 14):**
  the CPI-U index file vendored in the project's `data/` folder

```{r}
#| label: setup
### quarto runs chunks from this file's folder, so point them at the project root
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("../.."))
```

```{r}
#| label: shared-data
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

source("R/page-data.R")
source("R/cde-api.R")
source("analysis/marshall_requests/helpers.R")

### inputs that several slides share
pop <- read_us_population()
nps <- read_nps()
prisoners_2023 <- read_prisoners_2023()
prison_rate <- us_prison_rate(nps, prisoners_2023, pop)
recid <- read_recidivism()

### cde arrests come from the cache in data/, or the api when the cache is
### missing a year (needs DATA_GOV_API_KEY)
arrests <- read_cde_arrests(1985:2025)
latest_arrest_year <- max(arrests$year)

### 2021 is the fbi's switch to nibrs, when a quarter of the country didn't
### report arrests, so arrest trends skip it and the line runs straight from 2020 to 2022
arrest_gap_year <- 2021

fmt_n <- function(x) comma(round(x))
```

## Slide 3: Crime is down

```{r}
#| label: slide-03
crime <- us_crime_rates() |>
  filter(series != "Property crime")
crime_latest <- max(crime$year)
crime_change <- crime |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(first = value[year == first_year], last = value[year == crime_latest], .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(change = pct_change(first, last))

### panel names carry the % change, so the slide doesn't need a callout
crime_panels <- crime |>
  left_join(crime_change, by = "series") |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(series, " (", pct_label(change), ")"))
crime_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue")], unique(crime_panels$panel))

crime_chart <- trend_panels(crime_panels, crime_colors) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Crimes Reported per 100,000 Residents, ", first_year, "–", crime_latest),
    caption = slide_caption(
      "All crime is violent crime (homicide, rape, robbery, aggravated assault)",
      "plus property crime (burglary, larceny, motor vehicle theft).",
      source = "FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, state crime estimates."
    )
  )
save_slide(crime_chart, "slide-03-crime-rates")
crime_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-03-key-numbers
all_crime <- filter(crime_change, series == "All crime")
violent_crime <- filter(crime_change, series == "Violent crime")
```

- **All crime:** `r fmt_n(all_crime$first)` per 100,000 in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(all_crime$last)` in `r crime_latest`.
  That is `r pct_label(all_crime$change)`.
- **Violent crime:** `r fmt_n(violent_crime$first)` per 100,000 in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(violent_crime$last)` in `r crime_latest`.
  That is `r pct_label(violent_crime$change)`.

## Slide 4: Arrests are down

```{r}
#| label: slide-04
arrest_counts <- read_fbi_arrest_estimates() |>
  filter(year >= first_year, year != arrest_gap_year) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "series", values_to = "value")
estimate_latest <- max(arrest_counts$year)
arrest_change <- arrest_counts |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(first = value[year == first_year], last = value[year == estimate_latest], .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(change = pct_change(first, last))

arrest_panels <- arrest_counts |>
  left_join(arrest_change, by = "series") |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(series, " (", pct_label(change), ")"))
arrest_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue")], unique(arrest_panels$panel))

arrest_chart <- trend_panels(arrest_panels, arrest_colors) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Estimated Arrests in the U.S., ", first_year, "–", estimate_latest),
    caption = slide_caption(
      "The FBI's national arrest estimates. Drug arrests are drug abuse violations, including possession and sale.",
      paste0(arrest_gap_year, " is missing: the FBI published no national estimate during its switch to incident-based"),
      paste0("reporting (NIBRS). The line connects ", arrest_gap_year - 1, " and ", arrest_gap_year + 1, "."),
      source = "FBI, Crime in the United States, Estimated Number of Arrests (table 29), each year's release."
    )
  )
save_slide(arrest_chart, "slide-04-arrests")
arrest_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-04-key-numbers
all_arrests <- filter(arrest_change, series == "All arrests")
drug_arrests <- filter(arrest_change, series == "Drug arrests")
```

- **All arrests:** an estimated `r compact_label(all_arrests$first)` in `r first_year`,
  and `r compact_label(all_arrests$last)` in `r estimate_latest`.
  That is `r pct_label(all_arrests$change)`.
- **Drug arrests:** an estimated `r compact_label(drug_arrests$first)` in `r first_year`,
  and `r compact_label(drug_arrests$last)` in `r estimate_latest`.
  That is `r pct_label(drug_arrests$change)`.
- **Possible break in the series:** drug arrests before and after `r arrest_gap_year`
  come from two reporting systems. Some of the change across that line may come from
  the switch, not from policing.

## Slide 5: Racial disparities in arrests narrowed

```{r}
#| label: slide-05
acs_race <- read_acs_race()
rri <- arrest_rate_ratio(arrests, acs_race) |>
  filter(year >= first_year, year != arrest_gap_year) |>
  mutate(panel = "Black-to-White relative rate index")
acs_first <- min(acs_race$acs_year)
acs_latest <- max(acs_race$acs_year)

rri_chart <- trend_panels(rri, c(`Black-to-White relative rate index` = site_colors[["navy"]]),
                          label_fn = \(x) number(x, accuracy = 0.1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = site_colors[["baseline"]], linetype = "22") +
  annotate("text", x = first_year, y = 1, label = "Equal rates", vjust = -0.6, hjust = 0,
           family = chart_font, size = 3.2, color = site_colors[["muted"]]) +
  theme(strip.text = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Black-to-White Arrest Relative Rate Index, ", first_year, "–", latest_arrest_year),
    subtitle = "Black residents' arrest rate divided by White residents' arrest rate, all offenses",
    caption = slide_caption(
      paste0("Rates use non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White residents from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey ",
             "5-year estimates ending in each year (", acs_first - 4, "–", acs_first, " for years before ", acs_first,
             "; ", acs_latest - 4, "–", acs_latest, " for ", acs_latest + 1, ")."),
      "Race categories include people of any ethnicity, and many Latino people may be counted as White.",
      "Not enough law enforcement agencies collect ethnicity data to make reliable estimates for the Latino population.",
      paste0(arrest_gap_year, " is missing (NIBRS transition); the line connects ", arrest_gap_year - 1, " and ", arrest_gap_year + 1, "."),
      source = "FBI Crime Data Explorer, arrest data; U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B03002.",
      width = 155
    )
  )
save_slide(rri_chart, "slide-05-arrest-rate-ratio")
rri_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-05-key-numbers
rri_first <- number(rri$value[rri$year == first_year], accuracy = 0.1)
rri_last <- number(rri$value[rri$year == latest_arrest_year], accuracy = 0.1)
```

- **The relative rate index:** Black residents were arrested at `r rri_first` times the rate of White
  residents in `r first_year`, and `r rri_last` times in `r latest_arrest_year`.
- **Method:** the population base matches the data snapshot (non-Hispanic Black and White
  residents, ACS 5-year estimates). The snapshot's 2.7 is for property crime arrests in 2023;
  this slide uses all arrests.

## Slide 6: Fewer prison admissions

```{r}
#| label: slide-06
admissions <- nps |>
  filter(state_abbr == "ST", year >= first_year) |>
  transmute(year, `New court commitments` = new_court, `Supervision violations` = violations,
            technical = violation_technical) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`New court commitments`, `Supervision violations`), names_to = "series", values_to = "value")
admissions_latest <- max(admissions$year)
admission_colors <- c(`New court commitments` = site_colors[["navy"]],
                      `Supervision violations` = site_colors[["orange"]])

### end labels carry each line's change since the first year, as on slide 7
admission_names <- change_names(admissions)
admission_lines <- mutate(admissions, series = admission_names[series])
admission_line_colors <- setNames(admission_colors, admission_names[names(admission_colors)])

admissions_chart <- ggplot(admission_lines) +
  labeled_lines(admission_lines, admission_line_colors) +
  end_value_labels(admission_lines) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(first_year, admissions_latest, 5), expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = compact_label, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Admissions to State Prisons, ", first_year, "–", admissions_latest),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Supervision violations are admissions of people returned from parole or other",
      "conditional release, with or without a new sentence. BJS counts probation revocations as new court commitments.",
      "The 2020 drop reflects COVID-19 court and admission slowdowns.",
      source = "Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Prisoner Statistics, 1978–2022."
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(14, 230, 10, 14))
save_slide(admissions_chart, "slide-06-prison-admissions")
admissions_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-06-key-numbers
adm_ends <- admissions |>
  filter(year %in% c(first_year, admissions_latest)) |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(first = first(value), last = last(value),
            tech_first = first(technical), tech_last = last(technical), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(change = pct_change(first, last))
new_court <- filter(adm_ends, series == "New court commitments")
violations <- filter(adm_ends, series == "Supervision violations")
```

- **New court commitments:** `r fmt_n(new_court$first)` in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(new_court$last)` in `r admissions_latest`.
  That is `r pct_label(new_court$change)`.
- **Supervision violations:** `r fmt_n(violations$first)` in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(violations$last)` in `r admissions_latest`.
  That is `r pct_label(violations$change)`.
- **Technical violations alone** (returns with no new sentence):
  `r fmt_n(violations$tech_first)` in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(violations$tech_last)` in `r admissions_latest`.
- **Latest year:** BJS's file ends in `r admissions_latest`. The Prisoners 2023 report
  gives totals for 2023, but not by type of admission.

### 6b: Probation and parole violations

```{r}
#| label: slide-06b
### bjs counts probation revocations inside new court commitments, so probation
### comes from csg's state survey instead, for the states reporting every year
mclc <- read_mclc_violations()
mclc_states <- n_distinct(mclc$state_abbr)
mclc_lines <- mclc |>
  group_by(year, series) |>
  summarise(value = sum(value), .groups = "drop")
mclc_first <- min(mclc_lines$year)
mclc_latest <- max(mclc_lines$year)
mclc_colors <- c(`Probation violations` = site_colors[["navy"]], `Parole violations` = site_colors[["orange"]])

mclc_names <- change_names(mclc_lines)
mclc_plot <- mutate(mclc_lines, series = mclc_names[series])
mclc_line_colors <- setNames(mclc_colors, mclc_names[names(mclc_colors)])

### with one tick a year, the default nudge leaves a wide gap before the end labels
mclc_chart <- ggplot(mclc_plot) +
  labeled_lines(mclc_plot, mclc_line_colors, nudge_x = 0.15) +
  end_value_labels(mclc_plot) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = mclc_first:mclc_latest, expand = expansion(add = 0.3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = compact_label, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Prison Admissions for Supervision Violations, ", mclc_states, " States, ",
                   mclc_first, "–", mclc_latest),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Admissions to prison for a probation or parole violation, with or without a new offense.",
      paste0("Covers the ", mclc_states, " states that reported both every year; states define and count violations differently."),
      "The 2020 drop reflects COVID-19 court and admission slowdowns.",
      source = "CSG Justice Center, More Community, Less Confinement state survey."
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(14, 150, 10, 14))
save_slide(mclc_chart, "slide-06b-probation-parole-violations")
mclc_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-06b-key-numbers
mclc_ends <- mclc_lines |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(first = value[year == mclc_first], last = value[year == mclc_latest], .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(change = pct_change(first, last))
mclc_prob <- filter(mclc_ends, series == "Probation violations")
mclc_par <- filter(mclc_ends, series == "Parole violations")
mclc_prob_share <- mclc_prob$last / (mclc_prob$last + mclc_par$last)
```

- **Probation violations:** `r fmt_n(mclc_prob$first)` admissions in `r mclc_first` and
  `r fmt_n(mclc_prob$last)` in `r mclc_latest` across these `r mclc_states` states.
  That is `r pct_label(mclc_prob$change)`.
- **Parole violations:** `r fmt_n(mclc_par$first)` in `r mclc_first` and
  `r fmt_n(mclc_par$last)` in `r mclc_latest`. That is `r pct_label(mclc_par$change)`.
- **Probation's share:** `r percent(mclc_prob_share)` of these states' supervision violation
  admissions in `r mclc_latest`. The BJS line above leaves these out, since BJS counts
  probation revocations as new court commitments.

## Slide 7: Decline driven by youth violence

```{r}
#| label: slide-07
### all years, for the counts since 1995 in the bullets
youth_all_years <- youth_adult_violent(arrests, pop, read_us_youth_population())
youth <- youth_all_years |>
  filter(year >= first_year, year != arrest_gap_year)
youth_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("orange", "navy")], c(youth_series, adult_series))

### each line's end label carries its change since the first year; no rate labels
youth_names <- youth |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(name = paste0(
    first(series), ": ", pct_label(pct_change(value[year == first_year], value[year == latest_arrest_year]))
  ))
youth_lines <- youth |>
  left_join(youth_names, by = "series") |>
  mutate(series = name)
youth_line_colors <- setNames(youth_colors[youth_names$series], youth_names$name)

youth_chart <- ggplot(youth_lines) +
  labeled_lines(youth_lines, youth_line_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(first_year, latest_arrest_year, 5), expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Violent Crime Arrest Rates for Youth and Adults, ", first_year, "–", latest_arrest_year),
    subtitle = "Arrests per 100,000 residents in each age group",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Violent crime arrests are for homicide, rape, robbery, and aggravated assault.",
      "Youth rates use residents ages 10–17; youth arrests include the few children under 10.",
      "Counts are scaled to the full population by reporting coverage.",
      paste0(arrest_gap_year, " is missing (NIBRS transition); the line connects ", arrest_gap_year - 1, " and ", arrest_gap_year + 1, "."),
      source = "FBI Crime Data Explorer, arrest data; U.S. Census Bureau, population estimates."
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(14, 200, 10, 14))
save_slide(youth_chart, "slide-07-youth-adult-violent-arrests")
youth_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-07-key-numbers
youth_ends <- youth_all_years |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(
    rate_first = value[year == first_year], rate_last = value[year == latest_arrest_year],
    count_1995 = estimated[year == 1995], count_last = estimated[year == latest_arrest_year]
  ) |>
  mutate(rate_change = pct_change(rate_first, rate_last), count_change = pct_change(count_1995, count_last))
youth_row <- filter(youth_ends, series == youth_series)
adult_row <- filter(youth_ends, series == adult_series)
youth_faster <- youth_row$rate_change < adult_row$rate_change
```

- **Youth (ages 10–17):** `r fmt_n(youth_row$rate_first)` violent arrests per 100,000 in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(youth_row$rate_last)` in `r latest_arrest_year`.
  That is `r pct_label(youth_row$rate_change)`.
- **Adults (18 and older):** `r fmt_n(adult_row$rate_first)` per 100,000 in `r first_year`,
  and `r fmt_n(adult_row$rate_last)` in `r latest_arrest_year`.
  That is `r pct_label(adult_row$rate_change)`.
- **Which fell faster:** the youth rate fell `r if (youth_faster) "faster" else "more slowly"` than the adult rate.
  By `r latest_arrest_year`, youth were arrested for violent crime at
  `r if (youth_row$rate_last < adult_row$rate_last) "a lower" else "a higher"` rate than adults.
- **Since the 1995 peak:** the library has no population by age for the 1990s, so the chart starts in `r first_year`.
  Estimated violent arrest counts show the longer decline: youth arrests changed
  `r pct_label(youth_row$count_change)` from 1995 to `r latest_arrest_year`, and adult arrests
  `r pct_label(adult_row$count_change)`.

## Slide 8: State incarceration rates are down

```{r}
#| label: slide-08
peak <- slice_max(prison_rate, value, n = 1)
prison_latest <- slice_max(prison_rate, year, n = 1)
prison_change <- pct_change(peak$value, prison_latest$value)

prison_chart <- trend_panels(mutate(prison_rate, panel = "State prison rate"),
                             c(`State prison rate` = site_colors[["navy"]])) +
  slide_text(data = mutate(peak, panel = "State prison rate"),
             aes(year, value, label = paste0("Peak, ", year)),
             vjust = -1.3, size = 3.2, color = site_colors[["muted"]]) +
  ### under the end value, right of the line's last point, so it clears the line
  annotate("text", x = prison_latest$year + 0.5, y = prison_latest$value, vjust = 2.4, hjust = 0,
           label = paste0(pct_label(prison_change), " from peak"), family = chart_font,
           fontface = "bold", size = 3.6, color = site_colors[["navy"]]) +
  theme(strip.text = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("People in State Prison per 100,000 Residents, ", first_year, "–", prison_latest$year),
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Everyone under state prison jurisdiction at year end, per 100,000 U.S. residents,",
      "matching the CSG Justice Center data snapshots.",
      source = paste(
        "Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Prisoner Statistics (through 2022) and Prisoners in 2023;",
        "U.S. Census Bureau, population estimates."
      )
    )
  )
save_slide(prison_chart, "slide-08-state-prison-rate")
prison_chart
```

- **Rate:** `r round(peak$value)` per 100,000 residents at its `r peak$year` peak,
  and `r round(prison_latest$value)` in `r prison_latest$year`.
  That is `r pct_label(prison_change)`.
- **People in state prison:** `r fmt_n(peak$prison_pop)` at the peak,
  and `r fmt_n(prison_latest$prison_pop)` in `r prison_latest$year`.

## Slide 9: Fewer people going back to prison

Three versions of this slide follow:

- **9a** uses CSG's 50 States, 1 Goal data, 2010 onward.
- **9b** uses only BJS's national recidivism studies, which share one definition.
- **9c** puts the BJS and Pew studies on one timeline with the 50 States, 1 Goal trend.

The three sources count returns in similar but not identical ways, and each covers a
different set of states:

- **BJS** follows a sample of people released in one year from the states that sent
  records (15 to 23 states). It counts a return to prison for a new sentence or a
  supervision violation.
- **Pew** asked state corrections departments for the share of people released in 1999
  and 2004 who returned to prison, for a new crime or a technical violation, within three
  years.
- **50 States, 1 Goal** compiles each state's own published three-year reincarceration
  rate, so definitions vary somewhat by state.

### 9a: 50 States, 1 Goal

```{r}
#| label: slide-09a
recid_trend <- recidivism_trend(recid)
panel_label <- unique(recid_trend$series[recid_trend$series != "All reporting states"])
recid_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue")], c("All reporting states", panel_label))
recid_types <- setNames(c("solid", "22"), names(recid_colors))
recid_last <- max(recid_trend$year)
all_states_line <- filter(recid_trend, series == "All reporting states")
panel_line <- filter(recid_trend, series == panel_label)
thin <- filter(all_states_line, states < 30)

recid_chart <- ggplot(recid_trend) +
  labeled_lines(recid_trend, recid_colors, linetypes = recid_types) +
  ### the two lines start at the same point, so the dashed line only labels its end, below the line
  end_value_labels(all_states_line, label_fn = \(x) paste0(round(x), "%")) +
  slide_text(data = slice_max(panel_line, year, n = 1),
             aes(year, value, label = paste0(round(value), "%"), color = series), vjust = 2, size = 3.4) +
  ### how many states report each cohort, along the bottom
  slide_text(data = all_states_line, aes(year, 0, label = states),
             vjust = -0.8, size = 2.9, color = site_colors[["muted"]]) +
  annotate("text", x = min(recid_trend$year) - 0.6, y = 0, label = "States:", hjust = 1, vjust = -0.8,
           family = chart_font, size = 2.9, color = site_colors[["muted"]]) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, recid_last, 2), expand = expansion(add = 0.8)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Three-Year Reincarceration Rate by Release Year, 2010–", recid_last),
    subtitle = "Share of people released from state prison who returned within three years",
    x = "Year released", y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Rates are weighted by the number of people released in each state.",
      paste0("Fewer states have reported the latest cohorts (",
             paste0(thin$states, " for ", thin$year, collapse = ", "), "),"),
      "so the dashed line follows only the states with a rate for every cohort from 2010 to 2020.",
      "These cohorts end earlier than most other data in this presentation.",
      source = "CSG Justice Center, 50 States, 1 Goal state recidivism data."
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(14, 190, 10, 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(color = site_colors[["muted"]], size = 9.5))
save_slide(recid_chart, "slide-09-reincarceration")
recid_chart
```

- **Long view:** the national studies put three-year returns between

  `r round(panel_first$value)`% (`r panel_first$year`) to `r round(panel_last$value)`%
  (`r panel_last$year`), and BJS's 2012 study (`r bjs_last$rate`%) falls in line with that drop.

## Slide 13: Labor and health care drive costs

```{r}
#| label: slide-13
officers <- us_correctional_officers(nps, prisoners_2023)
wage_year <- max(officers$year)
staffing <- officers |>
  left_join(inflation_multiplier(wage_year), by = "year") |>
  mutate(wage_real = mean_wage * multiplier)
staff_change <- staffing |>
  summarise(wage_change = pct_change(first(wage_real), last(wage_real)),
            per_officer_first = first(per_officer),
            per_officer_last = last(na.omit(per_officer)),
            per_officer_last_year = max(year[!is.na(per_officer)]))

wage_panel <- paste0("Average pay, in ", wage_year, " dollars (", pct_label(staff_change$wage_change), ")")
officer_panel <- "People in state prison per correctional officer"
staff_panels <- staffing |>
  transmute(year, wage = wage_real, per_officer) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(panel = if_else(series == "wage", wage_panel, officer_panel))
staff_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue")], c(wage_panel, officer_panel))

### dollars for pay, one decimal for people per officer
staff_label <- \(x) if_else(x >= 1000, dollar(x, accuracy = 100), number(x, accuracy = 0.1, drop0trailing = TRUE))

staff_chart <- trend_panels(staff_panels, staff_colors, label_fn = staff_label,
                            years = range(staff_panels$year)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, wage_year, 2), expand = expansion(add = 0.8)) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Correctional Officers and Jailers: Pay and Workload, 2010–", wage_year),
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Pay is the average annual wage of correctional officers and jailers, adjusted for inflation. BLS publishes",
      "pay by state, so the national average weights each state by its number of officer jobs. Officer counts include local jails,",
      "so people per officer understates the prison workload.",
      source = "Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics; BJS prison counts."
    )
  )
save_slide(staff_chart, "slide-13-correctional-officers")
staff_chart
```

- **Average correctional officer pay, adjusted for inflation:**
  `r pct_label(staff_change$wage_change)` from 2010 to `r wage_year`.
- **People in state prison per correctional officer:**
  `r number(staff_change$per_officer_first, accuracy = 0.1)` in 2010,
  and `r number(staff_change$per_officer_last, accuracy = 0.1)` in `r staff_change$per_officer_last_year`.

### 13b: Correctional officer pay over time

```{r}
#| label: slide-13b
pay_names <- c(
  `Correctional Officers and Jailers` = "Correctional officers and jailers",
  `First-Line Supervisors of Correctional Officers` = "Their supervisors",
  Total = "All workers"
)
pay <- us_oews_pay(names(pay_names)) |>
  left_join(inflation_multiplier(wage_year), by = "year") |>
  mutate(occupation = pay_names[group], value = mean_wage * multiplier)
pay_change <- pay |>
  group_by(occupation) |>
  summarise(first = first(value), last = last(value), nominal_last = last(mean_wage), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(change = pct_change(first, last))

### line names carry the latest pay and the change since 2010, since value
### labels on lines this close would pile up
pay_lines <- pay |>
  left_join(select(pay_change, occupation, last, change), by = "occupation") |>
  mutate(series = paste0(occupation, ": ", dollar(last, accuracy = 100), " (", pct_label(change), ")"))
pay_series <- unique(pay_lines$series[order(match(pay_lines$occupation, pay_names))])
pay_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue", "slate")], pay_series)

pay_chart <- ggplot(pay_lines) +
  labeled_lines(pay_lines, pay_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, wage_year, 2), expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Average Pay of Correctional Officers, 2010–", wage_year),
    subtitle = paste0("Average yearly pay, in ", wage_year, " dollars"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "BLS publishes pay by state, so the national average weights each state's average by its number of jobs:",
      "states with more officers, like Texas and California, count more. Adjusted for inflation.",
      "Correctional officers and jailers include local jail staff. Supervisors are first-line supervisors",
      "of correctional officers. All workers is the average across every occupation, for comparison with",
      "pay in the wider labor market.",
      source = "Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2010–May 2024 state files."
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(14, 330, 10, 14))
save_slide(pay_chart, "slide-13b-officer-pay")
pay_chart
```

```{r}

all_pay <- filter(pay_change, occupation == "All workers")
```

- **Correctional officers and jailers:** average pay changed `r pct_label(officer_pay$change)`

  in `r wage_year`.
- **All workers:** `r pct_label(all_pay$change)` over the same years, to
  `r dollar(all_pay$nominal_last, accuracy = 100)` in `r wage_year`.

### 13c: CLA report Figure 14, rebuilt from BLS

*Workforce Trends in State Departments of Corrections: A 50-State Analysis* (February 2026),
by Michael Thompson, Katharine Teleki and Angela Gunter with the Correctional Leaders
Association, Figure 14 on page 27, shows average pay for state
corrections officers from 2017 to 2024 and reports a 33% increase. It cites the same BLS wage
tables. Its values are drawn as shapes in the PDF and can't be read as numbers, so this chart
rebuilds the figure from the BLS data above, in dollars of each year (not adjusted for inflation),
to match the report.

```{r}
#| label: slide-13c
cla_years <- 2017:wage_year
cla_pay <- pay |>
  filter(group == "Correctional Officers and Jailers", year %in% cla_years) |>
  select(year, mean_wage, states)
cla_change <- pct_change(first(cla_pay$mean_wage), last(cla_pay$mean_wage))

cla_chart <- ggplot(cla_pay, aes(factor(year), mean_wage)) +
  geom_col(fill = site_colors[["navy"]], width = 0.62) +
  slide_text(aes(label = dollar(mean_wage, accuracy = 100)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold",
             color = site_colors[["navy"]]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Average Pay for Correctional Officers, 2017–", wage_year),
    subtitle = paste0(pct_label(cla_change), " since 2017, not adjusted for inflation"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Average annual wage of correctional officers and jailers across states, weighted by jobs in each state.",
      "BLS state figures cover all employers, including local jails, so they differ a little from figures for",
      "state government alone. Thompson et al. (2026) found a 33% increase for state corrections officers",
      "over the same years.",
      source = paste(
        "Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics; Thompson et al., Workforce Trends",
        "in State Departments of Corrections (2026, with the Correctional Leaders Association), figure 14."
      )
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(color = site_colors[["text"]], size = 10.5),
        plot.margin = margin(14, 14, 10, 14))
save_slide(cla_chart, "slide-13c-officer-pay-cla")
cla_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-13c-key-numbers
officer_real <- filter(pay, group == "Correctional Officers and Jailers", year %in% range(cla_years))
cla_real_change <- pct_change(first(officer_real$value), last(officer_real$value))
```

- **Before inflation:** average pay rose from `r dollar(first(cla_pay$mean_wage), accuracy = 100)`
  in 2017 to `r dollar(last(cla_pay$mean_wage), accuracy = 100)` in `r wage_year`,
  `r pct_label(cla_change)`, close to the report's 33%.
- **After inflation:** pay rose only `r pct_label(cla_real_change)` over the same years.
  Most of the 2017–`r wage_year` raise kept pace with prices.

```{r}
stopifnot(length(health_states) == 1, !is.na(health_states))

health_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue")], unique(health_panels$panel))

### billions for the total, dollars for per person

      "year (no New Hampshire or North Dakota data). Pew adjusted for inflation with the GDP price deflator.",

    )
```

```{r}

```

- **Total spending:** across `r health_states` states, `r health_label(health_total$first)` in fiscal 2010 and
  `r health_label(health_total$last)` in fiscal 2015, in 2015 dollars.
  That is `r pct_label(health_total$change)`.
- **Median spending per person:** `r dollar(health_median$first)` in fiscal 2010 and
  `r dollar(health_median$last)` in fiscal 2015. That is `r pct_label(health_median$change)`.

## Slide 14: Fewer people, higher cost per person

```{r}
#| label: slide-14
nasbo <- read_nasbo_corrections()
spend_year <- max(nasbo$year)
spending <- nasbo |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(spending = sum(corrections, na.rm = TRUE), states = sum(!is.na(corrections)), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(year >= first_year) |>
  ### dollars of the chart's last year, as on every inflation-adjusted slide
  left_join(inflation_multiplier(spend_year), by = "year") |>
  left_join(select(prison_rate, year, prison_pop), by = "year") |>
  mutate(spending_real = spending * multiplier, per_person = spending_real / prison_pop)
spend_change <- spending |>
  summarise(total = pct_change(first(spending_real), last(spending_real)),
            per_person = pct_change(first(per_person), last(per_person)),
            pop = pct_change(first(prison_pop), last(prison_pop)))

spend_panels <- spending |>
  transmute(year, total = spending_real, per_person) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(panel = if_else(
    series == "total",
    paste0("Total state corrections spending (", pct_label(spend_change$total), ")"),
    paste0("Spending per person in state prison (", pct_label(spend_change$per_person), ")")
  ))
spend_colors <- setNames(site_colors[c("navy", "blue")], unique(spend_panels$panel))

### billions for the total, dollars for per person
spend_label <- \(x) if_else(x >= 1e9, paste0("$", number(x / 1e9, accuracy = 0.1), "B"), dollar(x, accuracy = 100))

spend_chart <- trend_panels(spend_panels, spend_colors, label_fn = spend_label) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("State Corrections Spending, Total and per Person in Prison, ", first_year, "–", spend_year),
    subtitle = paste0("In ", spend_year, " dollars"),
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Spending is state operating spending on corrections from all fund sources, by state fiscal year,",
      "adjusted for inflation. Per-person spending divides it by everyone under state prison",
      "jurisdiction at year end. Corrections spending also covers probation, parole, and other programs,",
      "so per-person figures are an upper bound.",
      source = "NASBO State Expenditure Report; BJS National Prisoner Statistics."
    )
  )
save_slide(spend_chart, "slide-14-corrections-spending")
spend_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-14-key-numbers
per_person_last <- dollar(last(spending$per_person), accuracy = 100)
```

- **Total state corrections spending, adjusted for inflation:**
  `r pct_label(spend_change$total)` from `r first_year` to `r spend_year`.
- **People in state prison:** `r pct_label(spend_change$pop)` over the same years.
- **Spending per person in state prison:** `r pct_label(spend_change$per_person)`,
  to `r per_person_last` in fiscal `r spend_year`, in `r spend_year` dollars.
- **Latest year:** NASBO's file ends in fiscal `r spend_year`.

## Slide 16: Find your state on the map

```{r}
#| label: slide-16
#| fig-height: 4.6
hex <- read_hex_states()

### crime: latest violent crime rate per 100k
state_crime <- read_rds(jr_data_path("analysis", "fbi", "srs", "fbi_srs_estimated_crimes_state.rds")) |>
  filter(indicator == "Incidents reported", group %in% violent_offenses, year == max(year)) |>
  group_by(state_abbr = as.character(state_abbr)) |>
  summarise(value = 1e5 * sum(n) / first(pop_total), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(measure = paste0("Violent crime rate, ", crime_latest))

### incarceration: people in state prison per 100k residents, 2023
state_pop_2023 <- read_rds(jr_data_path("analysis", "census", "pep", "census_pep_state.rds")) |>
  filter(group == "Total", year == 2023) |>
  transmute(state_abbr = as.character(state_abbr), pop_total)
state_prison <- prisoners_2023 |>
  filter(!is.na(state_abbr)) |>
  left_join(state_pop_2023, by = "state_abbr") |>
  transmute(state_abbr, value = 1e5 * prison_pop / pop_total, measure = "State prison rate, 2023")

### recidivism: each state's latest three-year reincarceration rate
state_recid <- recid |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(state_abbr = state.abb[match(state_name, state.name)], value = recid_rate,
            cohort = year, measure = "Reincarceration rate, latest cohort")

measures <- bind_rows(state_crime, state_prison, state_recid) |>
  group_by(measure) |>
  mutate(status = tercile_status(value)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = unique(measure)))

map_data <- hex |>
  cross_join(tibble(measure = levels(measures$measure))) |>
  left_join(mutate(measures, measure = as.character(measure)), by = c("state_abbr", "measure")) |>
  mutate(status = factor(coalesce(as.character(status), "No data"), levels = names(status_colors)),
         measure = factor(measure, levels = levels(measures$measure)))
label_points <- map_data |>
  mutate(geometry = sf::st_centroid(geometry)) |>
  mutate(x = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], y = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2])

map_chart <- ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = status), color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(map_data, status == "No data"), fill = NA, color = site_colors[["border"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = label_points, aes(x, y, label = state_abbr, color = status %in% c("Leading", "Lagging")),
            family = chart_font, fontface = "bold", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 3) +
  ### outline the legend keys so the white "no data" key shows
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors, drop = FALSE, name = NULL,
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = site_colors[["border"]]))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = site_colors[["text"]]), guide = "none") +
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  labs(
    title = "Where States Stand on Crime, Incarceration, and Recidivism",
    subtitle = "Each measure splits states into thirds: lowest third leading, highest third lagging",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = slide_caption(
      "Recidivism uses each state's latest reported three-year reincarceration rate",
      "(most are the 2020 or 2021 release cohort). States without a rate are white.",
      source = paste(
        "FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, state crime estimates; Bureau of Justice Statistics,",
        "Prisoners in 2023; CSG Justice Center, 50 States, 1 Goal."
      )
    )
  ) +
  theme_slide() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(color = site_colors[["text"]], size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 14, 10, 14)
  )
save_slide(map_chart, "slide-16-state-map", height = 4.6)
map_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-16-key-numbers
### states leading or lagging on all three measures, a starting point for the
### composite label
status_wide <- measures |>
  select(state_abbr, measure, status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = status)
state_list <- function(status) {
  states <- status_wide |>
    filter(if_all(-state_abbr, \(x) x %in% status)) |>
    pull(state_abbr)
  if (length(states)) paste(sort(states), collapse = ", ") else "none"
}
all_leading <- state_list("Leading")
all_lagging <- state_list("Lagging")
```

- **Leading on all three:** `r all_leading`
- **Lagging on all three:** `r all_lagging`

## Slide 22: Missouri case study

```{r}
#| label: slide-22
missouri_jr <- read_drop_in("missouri-jr.csv", c("series", "year", "value"))
mo_2023 <- filter(prisoners_2023, state_abbr == "MO")

### missouri's justice reinvestment numbers win when that file is there;
### otherwise bjs counts stand in
missouri <- if (!is.null(missouri_jr)) {
  mutate(missouri_jr, panel = series)
} else {
  nps |>
    filter(state_abbr == "MO", year >= first_year) |>
    select(year, prison_pop, violations) |>
    bind_rows(tibble(year = 2023, prison_pop = mo_2023$prison_pop)) |>
    pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(panel = if_else(series == "prison_pop", "People in prison", "Admissions for supervision violations"))
}
mo_palette <- site_colors[c("navy", "orange", "blue", "slate")]
mo_colors <- setNames(mo_palette[seq_len(n_distinct(missouri$panel))], unique(missouri$panel))

mo_caption <- if (is.null(missouri_jr)) {
  slide_caption(
    "Supervision violation admissions are people returned to prison from parole or other conditional release,",
    "with or without a new sentence. People in prison is everyone under Missouri's prison jurisdiction at year end.",
    source = paste(
      "Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Prisoner Statistics (through 2022)",
      "and Prisoners in 2023 (2023 population only)."
    )
  )
} else {
  slide_caption(
    "Years are state fiscal years, ending June 30. People in prison is the June 30 count.",
    "Supervision violation admissions are probation revocations (including 120-day program returns)",
    "plus parole returns, for new offenses or technical violations.",
    "Missouri's Justice Reinvestment law (HB 1355) passed in 2018.",
    source = "Missouri Department of Corrections, Profile of the Institutional and Supervised Offender Population, FY2025 (tables 1.4 and 4.2)."
  )
}
mo_years <- range(missouri$year)

mo_chart <- trend_panels(missouri, mo_colors, years = mo_years) +
  ### mark the 2018 justice reinvestment law
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2018, color = site_colors[["baseline"]], linetype = "22") +
  annotate("text", x = 2018, y = 0, label = "JR law, 2018", angle = 90, hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.5,
           family = chart_font, size = 3, color = site_colors[["muted"]]) +
  ### a short series needs a tick every couple of years, not every five
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(mo_years[1], mo_years[2], if (diff(mo_years) < 12) 3 else 5),
                     expand = expansion(add = c(1, 0.12 * diff(mo_years) + 1))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Missouri: Prison Population and Supervision Violation Admissions, ",
                   min(missouri$year), "–", max(missouri$year)),
    caption = mo_caption
  )
save_slide(mo_chart, "slide-22-missouri")
mo_chart
```

```{r}
#| label: slide-22-key-numbers
#| results: asis
mo_change <- missouri |>
  group_by(panel) |>
  summarise(first_year = min(year), first = first(value), last_year = max(year), last = last(value),
            peak_year = year[which.max(value)], peak = max(value), .groups = "drop")

### one bullet per panel, since the panels change when the missouri file is added
for (i in seq_len(nrow(mo_change))) {
  r <- mo_change[i, ]
  cat("- **", r$panel, ":** ",
      fmt_n(r$first), " in ", r$first_year, ", a peak of ", fmt_n(r$peak), " in ", r$peak_year,
      ", and ", fmt_n(r$last), " in ", r$last_year, ". ",
      "That is ", pct_label(pct_change(r$peak, r$last)), " from the peak.\n", sep = "")
}
if (is.null(missouri_jr)) {
  cat("- **Stand-in data:** this uses BJS figures until Missouri's Justice Reinvestment numbers",
      "are added as data/missouri-jr.csv.\n")
} else {
  cat("- **Why these differ from BJS:** Missouri DOC counts probation revocations, including 120-day",
      "program returns, as supervision violations, and uses fiscal years. BJS's National Prisoner",
      "Statistics counts fewer violation admissions and uses calendar years.\n")
}
```
